title: Self-correcting joint control under digital-twin mismatch
research_question: Does feeding measured junction temperatures back into the joint controller (one-sided offset-free correction) restore thermal safety under twin mismatch without giving up its energy advantage?
hypothesis: H1: in every mismatch case where joint exceeded the 80 C target, joint_robust has zero chip-seconds throttled and at least 80% fewer chip-seconds above target than joint. H2: joint_robust uses no more energy per successful task than independent (paired 95% CI upper bound <= 0) in every case. H3: with a correct twin (default and *_twin_correct variants), joint_robust is within +/-0.5% of joint on energy per successful task.
null_hypothesis: The correction does not remove overheating, or it removes it only by giving up the energy advantage.
baseline: independent within each case; joint within each case
configuration: Mismatch cases as E005, plus the registry default.
evaluation_criteria: Paired relative differences with 95% t-CI; practical threshold 1%; chip-second counts as seed means.
known_limitations: The correction only tightens the temperature target; it does not re-estimate leakage, so energy predictions stay biased.
disclosure: Before registration a unit test ran S3_hot (1 h, seed 0) with the leakage mismatch and showed joint_robust with fewer than half of joint's chip-seconds above target.
data_collection: Simulator outputs written to the append-only SQLite store; every metric labelled with provenance; per-run config SHA-256 and code SHA-256 recorded; time series for selected seeds.
statistics: Paired by seed (identical workload realisation across levels). Per-seed relative difference d=(A-B)/B; mean with two-sided 95% Student-t CI.
